title: Pyaaz Kachori

ingredients.name: Fennel seeds, coriander seeds, red chilli powder, amchur, garam masala
Oil or ghee for dough and deep frying

recipe: Knead a stiff dough with maida, salt, a little oil/ghee and water. Rest 20–30 minutes.
For filling: Heat oil, add fennel and coriander seeds, then finely chopped onion. Cook till golden. Add spice powders, green chillies, ginger and salt. Cool completely.
Divide dough into balls, stuff with onion mixture, seal and flatten slightly. Deep-fry on medium heat till golden and crisp.
Serve hot with tamarind and green chutneys.
tips: Jaipur and Jodhpur are famous for flaky pyaaz kachori.
Do not overcrowd the pan while frying for even crispness.

title: Mirchi Bada

ingredients.name: Amchur, red chilli powder, garam masala, coriander powder

recipe: Slit green chillies lengthwise and remove seeds if less heat is preferred.
Mash boiled potatoes with spice powders, amchur and salt. Stuff into the chillies.
Make a thick besan batter with water, salt and a pinch of chilli powder.
Dip stuffed chillies in batter and deep-fry till golden and crisp.
Serve hot with green chutney or tamarind chutney.
tips: A classic Rajasthani street breakfast and tea-time snack.
Choose milder large chillies for better balance.

title: Bajre ki Roti with Lehsun Chutney

ingredients.name: Red chilli powder, salt, lemon juice or amchur

recipe: Knead bajra flour with hot water and salt into a soft dough. Divide and pat into thick rotis with wet hands.
Cook on a hot tawa on both sides, then finish on open flame if possible for charred spots.
For lehsun chutney: Pound or grind garlic with red chilli powder, salt and a little water or lemon. Adjust spice.
Serve hot bajra roti smeared with ghee alongside the garlic chutney.
tips: Bajra is a desert staple and highly nutritious.
Eat the roti fresh as it hardens on cooling.

title: Dal Baati Churma

ingredients.name: Toor dal + chana dal + moong dal (mixed)
Jaggery or powdered sugar, cardamom (for churma)
Cumin, asafoetida, red chilli, turmeric, garam masala

recipe: For baati: Knead wheat flour with salt, a little ghee and water into a stiff dough. Shape into round balls, make a small dent, and bake in a traditional oven, tandoor or modern oven till hard and golden. Dip in melted ghee.
For dal: Pressure-cook mixed dals. Temper with cumin, hing, chilli and spices. Simmer to desired consistency.
For churma: Crush a few baked baatis, roast with ghee, mix powdered jaggery/sugar and cardamom.
Serve baati cracked open and soaked in ghee with dal and sweet churma on the side.
tips: The iconic Rajasthani trinity. Traditionally baatis were baked in sand or embers.
Generous ghee is essential for authentic taste.

title: Gatte ki Sabzi

ingredients.name: Red chilli powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, ajwain
Oil or ghee, cumin, asafoetida, curry leaves

recipe: Mix besan with spices, ajwain, salt and a little oil/yogurt to form a stiff dough. Shape into long cylinders (gatte). Boil in water 12–15 minutes till they float. Cool and slice into rounds.
Whisk yogurt with spice powders. Temper cumin, hing and optional onion/tomato in oil/ghee. Add the yogurt mixture and cook on low heat till it thickens (stir continuously to avoid curdling).
Add the gatte pieces and simmer 5–7 minutes. Adjust consistency with water.
Serve with roti, bajra roti or rice.
tips: A signature Rajasthani dish that uses no fresh vegetables – perfect for the desert climate.
Jain versions omit onion and garlic.

title: Ker Sangri

ingredients.name: Red chilli powder, turmeric, coriander powder, amchur, garam masala
Mustard oil or ghee, cumin, asafoetida

recipe: Soak ker and sangri in water for at least 4–6 hours or overnight. Drain and rinse well.
Pressure-cook or boil till soft. Drain.
Heat mustard oil till smoking, cool slightly. Temper cumin and hing. Add the ker-sangri, spice powders and salt. Sauté on medium heat till well coated and slightly dry.
Finish with amchur. Serve with bajra roti or regular roti.
tips: Iconic desert dish made from local hardy plants that grow in arid conditions.
Has a unique tangy-spicy flavour and long shelf life.

title: Laal Maas

ingredients.name: Mathania red chillies or Kashmiri + hot red chillies
Ghee or oil, whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves)

recipe: Soak red chillies and grind to a fine paste. Marinate mutton with yogurt, chilli paste, salt and ginger-garlic for at least 1 hour.
Heat ghee, add whole spices and sliced onion. Cook till golden. Add the marinated mutton and sear well.
Add a little water, cover and slow-cook (or pressure-cook) till mutton is tender and the gravy turns deep red and thick.
Finish with a tempering of ghee and garlic if desired. Serve with bajra roti, missi roti or rice.
tips: The signature fiery red colour and heat come from Mathania chillies.
A royal Rajput dish traditionally cooked with minimal water.

title: Safed Maas

ingredients.name: Yogurt, cashew paste, poppy seed paste, almond paste
Onion, ginger-garlic, green cardamom, white pepper

recipe: Marinate mutton with yogurt, salt and ginger-garlic.
Heat ghee, add whole spices and sliced onion. Cook till soft but not browned (to keep the gravy white).
Add the mutton and cook. Stir in cashew, poppy and almond pastes. Add water or stock and simmer till tender.
Finish with white pepper and a little cream if desired. The gravy should remain pale.
Serve with roti or rice.
tips: The ‘white’ counterpart to Laal Maas – mild, rich and nutty.
Royal court influence is evident in the use of dry fruits and dairy.

title: Bedmi Poori

ingredients.name: Fennel, coriander seeds, red chilli, asafoetida, ginger

recipe: Mix wheat flour with the spiced urad dal paste, salt and a little oil. Knead into a stiff dough. Rest 20 minutes.
Roll into small pooris and deep-fry till puffed and golden.
Serve hot with aloo sabzi or kadhi.
tips: Also popular in parts of UP and Rajasthan as a breakfast or snack.
The urad dal makes the poori flavourful and slightly crisp.

title: Bikaneri Bhujia

ingredients.name: Moth dal flour or besan + moth flour
Salt, oil for dough and frying

recipe: Mix the flour with spice powders, salt and a little oil. Add water to form a soft, pipeable dough.
Heat oil. Using a sev press or bhujia maker with fine holes, extrude the dough directly into hot oil in circular motions.
Fry till crisp and light golden. Drain and cool completely.
Store in airtight containers.
tips: GI-tagged specialty of Bikaner.
The unique peppery flavour distinguishes it from regular sev.

title: Panchmel Dal

ingredients.name: Five dals (toor, chana, moong, urad, masoor)
Turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder, garam masala, amchur
Cumin, asafoetida, dry red chilli, ghee

recipe: Wash and pressure-cook the five dals with turmeric till soft. Mash lightly.
Temper ghee with cumin, hing and dry red chilli. Add the cooked dal, remaining spices and salt. Simmer 5–7 minutes.
Adjust consistency. Finish with a spoon of pure ghee.
Serve with baati, roti or rice.
tips: Panchmel means five-mix – a classic Rajasthani mixed dal.
Often served as part of dal-baati.

title: Papad ki Sabzi

ingredients.name: Red chilli powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala

recipe: Break papads into pieces. Lightly roast or fry if desired.
Whisk yogurt with spice powders. Temper cumin and hing in ghee. Add the yogurt mixture and cook on low heat, stirring continuously.
Add papad pieces and a little water. Simmer 3–4 minutes till papads soften but do not disintegrate completely.
Serve with roti or bajra roti.
tips: A clever desert dish that turns preserved papad into a curry.
Cook briefly so papads retain some texture.

title: Kalmi Vada

ingredients.name: Fennel, coriander seeds, red chilli, ginger, green chilli

recipe: Soak moong dal for 3–4 hours. Drain and grind coarsely with spices and salt (do not make a fine paste).
Shape into small flat discs or logs.
Deep-fry on medium heat till crisp and golden.
Serve with green chutney or as a tea-time snack.
tips: A traditional Rajasthani dal-based snack.
Coarse texture gives the characteristic bite.

title: Kadhi Kachori

ingredients.name: Cumin, mustard, fenugreek seeds, dry red chilli, curry leaves

recipe: Prepare or use ready spicy kachoris.
For kadhi: Whisk yogurt with besan, turmeric, chilli powder and water. Cook on medium heat, stirring, till it thickens and the raw smell disappears.
Temper with cumin, mustard, fenugreek, dry red chilli and curry leaves in ghee. Pour over the kadhi.
Serve hot kadhi with kachoris dipped or on the side.
tips: A popular Rajasthani breakfast combination, especially in Jaipur and Ajmer.
The kadhi is usually thinner than Gujarati or Punjabi versions.
